newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NFI Octava shows '96 loss, sees '97 profit.
newsitem.headline: Polish NFI Octava shows '96 loss, sees '97 profit.

text.p: Polish NFI 8 Octava had a net 72 million zloty loss in 1996, following a creation of risk provisions for firms in its portfolio, but it expects to show profit in 1997, an official of the firm managing the fund said.
Czeslaw Obodzinski, finance director of KP Konsorcjum Sp z oo, told a news briefing on Monday the fund was likely to show profits in the first quarter of 1997, but declined to give details.
The fund had an audited net loss of 23 million zlotys for the nine months to December 31, 1995.

"According to unaudited results we had about 72-million- zloty loss (in 1996), mainly because of provisions made in our firms. Between 60 and 70 percent of the loss is due to the provisions, while some firms had very good operating results," he said.
"The first quarter looks very good...preliminary results in our companies are good and the fund will have profit this year," he added, but declined to give any figures.
He said the fund would publish audited 1996 results in June.
KP Konsorcjum president Martin Miszerak, also present, said the companies in the fund's portfolio improved their operating margin to average three percent in 1996 from 1.7 percent in 1995.
"The three percent last year is still not satisfactory, but it's a good sign," he said and added that the companies were likely to show higher margin this year.
